the current-current hadronic operator evolution is dominated by the non-perturbative contributions, that these contributions are large and negative, and that the current-current operator is suppressed at large distances.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the chiral and large- N limits, current-current operator evolution is dominated by a single scale, which can be interpreted as the confinement scale, and is insensitive to the details of the low-energy effective theory.

the current-current operator evolution is dominated by perturbative QED-like contributions in the ultraviolet region while it is dominated by non-linear σ-model-like contributions in the infrared region.
the current-current operator evolution in massless QCD can be computed with an accuracy of 10% for the relevant momentum range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current-current operator evolution in QCD is very different from that in the non-linear σ-model.
the strong interaction corrections are small and that the chiral limit is well defined for current-current operators.

the current-current operator is not a good probe of the QCD vacuum at large distance, and that its evolution with the scale should not be trusted beyond the scale where it is matched with the non-linear σ-model.
